title: Hanae Mori's birth chart
metaDescription: Hanae Mori's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 17.1° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is an opposition: Venus and Neptune within 0.1°, taste wired to imagination. Across the wheel, each body sees the other in full. The old reading is not conflict so much as permanent mutual visibility.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 17.1° Capricorn — the second decan, 10°–20°, which the tradition sub-rules by Venus. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Capricorn and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Sagittarius (25.8°), Venus in Aquarius (24.2°), Mars in Sagittarius (7.6°): a mind that decides at speaking speed, taste led by wit and proportion, drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Venus opposition Neptune, 0.1° of separation. Across the wheel, each body sees the other in full. The old reading is not conflict so much as permanent mutual visibility. Behind it, Venus square Saturn at 0.8°, and Saturn square Neptune at 0.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Venus opposes Neptune while both square Saturn. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, one sits in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Sagittarius at 25.8° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 3 fire, 3 water, 2 air, 1 earth by element and 4 fixed, 3 mutable, 2 cardinal by modality. A fire-weighted chart runs hot at the start line — initiative is its native language. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Libra into Scorpio during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.8° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
